Chapter 9: Sustaining the Practice and Embracing Change
You know, death cleaning isn’t just something you do once and forget about. It’s really an ongoing practice—because life keeps moving. We have new experiences, our relationships shift, and let’s be honest, stuff keeps finding its way into our homes.
When you make mindful decluttering part of your routine, you give yourself the gift of order and ease that lasts through the years. It’s not about perfection—it’s about helping your space reflect where you are right now.
Want to keep things manageable? Try doing a quick check-in every so often. Maybe once a season, or after something big happens in your life. These moments are perfect for making sure your things still match your needs and values. That way, you won’t wake up one day buried under a mountain of stuff you don’t even remember collecting.
Here are a few simple ways you can keep the momentum going:
Set yourself a recurring reminder—maybe pick one area to review each month. It could be a drawer, a closet, or even your digital files.
Bring your family into the process. Decluttering together can turn into a meaningful tradition, and it’s a great way to connect and share stories as you sort through memories.
Take a moment to reflect on your values and priorities as they shift over time. Let your home change with you, so it always feels like it truly belongs to you.
And don’t forget to celebrate the wins, no matter how small. Recognize the freedom and clarity you’re creating, step by step.
Embracing change is a big part of this journey. As you grow and your circumstances evolve, your relationship with your things will naturally shift too. If you stay tuned in to what matters most, you’ll keep building a home—and a legacy—that’s a real reflection of your truest self.
